name: HVAC Edge Control Plane architecture adjudication

authority.project: User adjudication over SE-ARCH-004 V2.1.2 and SE-ARCH-DEPLOY-001 V1.0 CURRENT
authority.principle: No architecture wins by incumbency. For each concern, adopt the design that is simpler, safer, more predictable and more maintainable for commercial HVAC. OPENEMS means adopt the stronger OpenEMS mechanism after reviewing pinned official source, tests and docs; it does not require copying Java/OSGi source code.

verdictLegend.OPENEMS: OpenEMS design is superior for this concern; adopt its architectural semantics and replace conflicting HVAC design.
verdictLegend.HVAC: Current HVAC design is superior for this concern; retain it as the target.
verdictLegend.MERGE: Neither side is sufficient alone; combine the stronger parts into one target design.
verdictLegend.REJECT: Do not make this implementation choice part of the target architecture.

targetEdgeRuntime.name: HVAC Edge Control Plane
targetEdgeRuntime.cloudCommandSemantics: durable governed intent, not direct actuator ownership

sourceValidation.policy: Existing local implementation has no incumbency preference. A module is VERIFIED only after pinned OpenEMS source, relevant upstream tests and local behavior have been compared. Material conflicts default to OpenEMS behavior unless an evidence-backed HVAC justification is recorded.

decisions.target: Edge owns fast local closed-loop control; Cloud owns policy, governance and long-horizon intent.
Keep current Cloud/Edge isolation and extend it so local controllers, schedules and safety continue without Cloud.
Explicitly prohibit soft-real-time Edge software from replacing PLC, fire, trip or equipment protection logic.
Adopt an explicit Input -> Process -> Output Edge cycle.
All controllers in one cycle read the same immutable process image.
Asynchronous device reads update nextValue; cycle boundary promotes nextValue to value.
Protocol I/O must not block controller execution and must synchronize through cycle events/boundaries.
Introduce a reusable Edge Controller interface executed every cycle with bounded runtime and explicit failure state.
Introduce deterministic ordered controller execution.
Higher-priority controllers constrain feasible outputs; later controllers cannot overwrite established limits.
Keep durable Cloud Command lifecycle but treat dispatched commands as Edge intents that participate in local arbitration.

decisions.concern: Durable command lifecycle, approval and audit
decisions.target: Retain SUBMITTED/VALIDATING/APPROVAL/DISPATCH/VERIFY terminal lifecycle, IAM authorization and audit as Cloud authority.
Edge performs immediate local readback/constraint verification; Cloud retains durable authoritative command outcome verification.
Remote setpoints/intents have an expiry or lease; stale Cloud control must relinquish to local control.
Move dynamic safety/interlock enforcement to reusable local controllers while retaining Cloud policy/audit evidence.
Point remains the canonical platform data-point identity.
Introduce Channel as the live Edge runtime value object with type, unit, access, quality and priority metadata.
Every governed Edge Channel maps to a canonical Point; Channel addresses never replace Point identity.
Retain independent Asset, Device Endpoint, optional physical Sensor, Point and versioned bindings.
Introduce Capability Profile as HVAC equivalent of Nature; controllers depend on capabilities, not vendor drivers.
Capability Profiles declare required and optional Channels/Points plus command limits.
Introduce local component registry for drivers, bridges, controllers, channels and services.
Introduce Edge Manifest derived/reconciled with Cloud Registry; expose capabilities/channels/drivers/controllers without making Edge config the Cloud master-data authority.
Vendor/product-specific logic lives in Device Drivers behind capability interfaces.
Connection lifecycle, retries, serialization and transport pooling belong to reusable Modbus/BACnet/OPC-UA/MQTT Bridges, not each driver.
Drivers primarily declare register/object mappings, conversion and write rules instead of hand-building transport loops.
Protocol reads have explicit priority/frequency so critical state is polled more often than diagnostics.
Channel access RO/RW/WO is derived from Point authority/writable semantics and driver capability.
Driver exposes implemented Capability Profiles and limits; Cloud Registry reconciles rather than infers from vendor name.
Keep MQTT over TLS as canonical Edge-Cloud transport; do not replace it with OpenEMS Backend WebSocket.
Introduce local latest/history service independent from a failed MQTT publish queue.
Keep current persistent queue semantics and integrate them with Edge Timedata/resend cursors.
Channels/Points carry persistence priority controlling regular Cloud transmission.
Perform selected time aggregation on Edge to reduce Cloud/database load while preserving raw policy for required points.
Replay prioritizes critical state/fault/control evidence over low-value diagnostics.

decisions.concern: Change-based publication plus periodic full snapshot
decisions.target: Publish changes promptly and periodically emit a complete snapshot for convergence/recovery.

decisions.concern: Cloud historical telemetry and analytics authority
decisions.target: Retain S2/ClickHouse/PostgreSQL split; OpenEMS Timedata does not replace Cloud analytical architecture.
Simulated and real devices differ at Driver/Protocol boundary, not in Controller/Command/Telemetry business logic.
Support both independent data-source devices and reacting physical models affected by control outputs.
Simulator models ramp, startup/shutdown delay, minimum run/stop, fault, timeout, stale data, noise, stuck actuator and rejected writes.
Device-driver tests can run against simulated Modbus/BACnet/etc endpoints, not only direct in-memory device models.
Single-equipment controller owns local sequence/state transitions and device-specific control behavior.
Plant/cluster controller allocates load/modes across equipment; single controllers remain responsible for individual equipment state machines.
Adopt scheduler concept for future HVAC mode scheduling, adapted to thermal/plant constraints rather than ESS-specific equations.
Heavy forecasting/global optimization may run in Cloud; Edge executes versioned schedules and preserves local fallback/safety when disconnected.
Retain Tenant/Site/Role/Policy IAM and database RLS as Cloud authorization authority.
Retain Space/Asset/Device/Sensor/Point identity, binding history, calibration/provenance and product-facing Asset model.
Retain Cloud alarm lifecycle, work management and durable audit; Edge emits evidence/events but does not replace these domains.
Generate Asset controls from Registry + Capability Profile + Edge Manifest while retaining HVAC Asset-centered UX.

decisions.concern: Direct transplant of OpenEMS Java/OSGi Backend/UI runtime
decisions.target: Adopt proven architectural mechanisms without making Java/OSGi/OpenEMS Backend/UI a target dependency. A bounded runtime PoC may still be used for evidence, but implementation technology must earn its place independently.

implementationPhases.P1: Edge foundation required before claiming production-grade controllable HVAC Edge
implementationPhases.P2: Plant-level composition, aggregation and dynamic UI

conformance.reason: S10 verifies the source-aligned Channel, Process Image, Cycle, Controller/Scheduler/Arbiter, Capability/Component/Manifest, local Timedata, lease and simulator/physical Driver contract foundation. The target remains PARTIAL because a concrete real Protocol Bridge/driver path, protocol-level simulation, historic resend/live convergence, governed Cloud readback and fleet/signed-release lifecycle are not yet complete.
